Checked set-builder selection, conjunction, permutation/ranking interpretation, comparison inequality, snapshot subscripts, and prose definitions for balanced syntax and consistent meaning.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates authorization, noncompensable fitness, index scope, ranking, temporal state, and coverage limits.

evidence: Executed catalog-eligibility-before-ranking and matched legacy popularity-first selection, false suitability, one eligible finance.orders_product result, and final product selection exactly.

Recomputed that legacy popularity 1000 exceeds product popularity 100, while its 1,440-minute freshness and failed contract/quality conditions violate the 60-minute contracted/approved eligibility requirement.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic fixture correctly demonstrates that rank order over raw matches cannot replace eligibility filtering.

evidence: Verified C(q,u,t) includes only entities in the catalog snapshot satisfying both authorization and fitness predicates.
Verified ranking is a permutation/order of C and therefore cannot expand the eligible set.
Confirmed unknown authorization or required evidence is omitted/held under policy, and search completeness is explicitly bounded by source coverage, authorization and snapshot time.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Formal claims preserve candidate-set membership, ranking scope, user/use context, temporal snapshot and unknown-state premises.

evidence: Traced stable entity identity, provenance assertions, rebuildable projections, authorization, eligibility, rank, result explanation, certification, access receipt, role ownership, index/source freshness and lifecycle through exposition, examples, and answers.

Confirmed authorization precedes every discovery surface, eligibility precedes ranking, access approval remains separate from enforcement, and catalog-local edits cannot silently replace source authority.
Confirmed active actions re-read current state/policy and use scoped preview, authorization, version preconditions, idempotency, receipts and reconciliation.
invariant_checking.notes: No crawl, index, match, popularity, click, semantic similarity, documentation score, badge, owner display, access approval, green page, or adoption metric is described as broader evidence than it supplies.

evidence: Reviewed the seven-step counterexample with popularity 1,000 versus 100 and shared lexical/technical orders match.
Confirmed legacy fails freshness, contract and quality eligibility while popularity-first ranks it above the current product.
Confirmed eligibility-first removes legacy and permits popularity only among suitable results.
proof_review.notes: The counterexample validly disproves a guarantee of fitness from popularity-first ranking over raw matches.

evidence: The popularity counterexample is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
The following limitation preserves popularity as a possible signal among eligible products while noting bias/context.
The executable is explicitly scoped away from search, semantic, identity, policy, access and universal-ranking behavior.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Proof, policy requirement, ranking heuristic, deterministic fixture and limitations remain distinct.

evidence: Current vocabulary, search/discovery, graph/index architecture, catalog workflow, entity model, contract and runtime identity behavior is attributed to dated primary sources.
Popularity/clicks, semantic similarity, inferred/generated metadata, access logs, source/index freshness and catalog coverage are labeled as evidence with bias or scope limits.
Certification, quality, access, eligibility and authorization are represented as versioned policy/evidence decisions rather than empirical universal truth.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Standards, implementation documentation, deterministic illustration, behavior signals, inference, policy and authoritative decisions are labeled distinctly.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It integrates user jobs, stable entity/assertion models, rebuildable graph/search projections, authorization-before-retrieval, eligibility-before-ranking, evidence-bearing entity pages, separate access enforcement, certification/stewardship/lifecycle workflows, guarded actions, relevance evaluation and source-to-index operability without treating inventory or popularity as trust.
